Before meeting Nigrodha Sāmaṇera, the king worshipped and offered alms to the naked ascetics (Ajivikas).
The young novice the king saw was calm and composed, wearing his robe neatly, walking mindfully without stumbling, and holding his alms bowl with eyes lowered.
The king admired the young novice because of his calm and composed behavior, neatly worn robe, steady mindful walking, and humble way of receiving alms.

After meeting the young novice, the king’s mind and actions changed. The once cruel and violent ruler became gentle, calm, and ruled his people justly.

Reason for the change: It was because he listened to the Dhamma preached by the young novice and understood the truth.
King Asoka seized the throne of India by killing his own brothers.

To be calm and full of spiritual faculties (Indriya), live with mindfulness, self-discipline, and virtue. Control your senses, act with moderation, cultivate patience and generosity, understand reality clearly, and maintain balance in life. This builds inner steadiness and wisdom.
The king's name is King Asoka, and he ruled India.
